_comment: C0-9 正文英译 · grafana-mcp（2026-10-25）。无 extraSections（内置五节由 axes/leads/runs/unknowns/related 承载）。

axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — an interface implementation called by MCP clients. It wraps your Grafana instance
(dashboards, data sources, alerts, OnCall/IRM etc.) as tools for agents.
axes.local_files:
Reads and writes no local files — the scope is the Grafana instance and its connected data sources;
unified-SQL credentials are handled by data source configuration, the official README states the server never sees the credentials.
axes.background: stdio lives and dies with the client; no background-task semantics.
axes.tools:
Dashboard family (search/read/summary/JSONPath property extraction/update/create/patch), data source family,
unified SQL (ClickHouse/Snowflake/Athena/MySQL/PostgreSQL/MSSQL),
the Prometheus/Loki/CloudWatch/Elasticsearch query families, Cloud Logging, the RBAC and user-management families;
some tool groups (running panel queries, query examples, Graphite) are **disabled by default**, enable with --enabled-tools.
The complete inventory follows the repo README.
axes.context:
No server-side cross-session memory — state lives in the Grafana instance itself.
The official README warns specifically: full dashboard JSON eats the context window,
prefer the window-saving tools summary/JSONPath/patch.
axes.permissions:
**The permission surface is the core of this entry**: Grafana service account token + fine-grained RBAC scopes
(the official README lists the minimum action per tool); the README also gives a convenience note — the built-in Editor role
is coarser than hand-made scopes, use it only when "convenience matters more than least privilege".
The SSE/streamable-http line can set separate caller authentication (--server-auth-token); stdio is unaffected.
axes.fit:
Fits: agents querying dashboards/metrics/alerts, modifying dashboards, and running cross-data-source unified SQL
on self-hosted or Grafana Cloud instances.
Not a fit: zero-config tokenless scenarios (a service account token is required); Grafana below 9.0 (some features missing).

mcp.transport:
**stdio** (uvx mcp-grafana) is primary; the official line also provides an SSE/streamable-http server mode
(with optional caller auth). Verified: repo README (fetched directly 2026-10-23).
mcp.auth:
Server side connects to Grafana with GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN; client side optional
--server-auth-token Bearer (only effective for SSE/streamable-http).
Official README: when caller auth is enabled, validated Authorization headers are stripped before reaching Grafana.
mcp.scope:
Both read and write: dashboard reads + update/create/patch, alert and IRM lines have write actions;
the minimum RBAC action per tool is listed in the README. SQL credentials go through data source configuration, the server never handles them.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The full tool inventory and the per-tool RBAC action mapping (the README has lists, not enumerated item by item)
- The current usage surface of the SSE/streamable-http server mode (the README explains the mode; the official side provides no hosted endpoint)
- The functional boundaries of the Docker/Helm deployment lines (not verified item by item)
related: Both observability surfaces: Sentry focuses on error-issue triage, Grafana is the dashboard and data-source query surface.
Same-category contrast: Grafana is open source and self-hostable, Datadog is closed source with official hosting plus credential pass-through.
